QF.id: Retirement Planning Products: National Pension System (NPS)_100

question.text: Amit has NPS Tier I corpus of Rs.30 lakh at age 60. He wants maximum lump sum. How much must he allocate to annuity at minimum?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XVII (pp.110, 120-122), normal NPS exit at age 60 requires a minimum 40% annuitization. 40% of Rs.30 lakh = Rs.12 lakh, with the remaining Rs.18 lakh (60%) available as a tax-free lump sum. The Trap: The 80% annuity requirement applies to premature exit, not normal exit at 60. The Rs.5 lakh full-lump-sum rule does not apply here because the corpus exceeds that threshold. Note: Walk clients through the 40%/60% split before retirement so they can plan their post-retirement cash flow; actual monthly pension from the annuity will depend on the annuity option selected and the prevailing annuity rate.
